summary: Reverse DNS PTR probes blocked by egress appliance causing OCSP/client-cert revocation validation delays and intermittent control-plane mTLS failures
description:
Issue summary:
Customers on Acadia's Private deployment experienced intermittent control-plane authentication failures (mTLS) and 502/403s when fetching presigned shards. Symptoms coincided with spikes in token refresh failures and OCSP responder timeouts. Root cause appears tied to reverse DNS (PTR) probes initiated by an egress NAT appliance that are being blocked/blackholed by the corporate perimeter, causing delays in upstream TLS certificate revocation/OCSP stapling validation and client-cert verification paths.

Impact:
- Intermittent model artifact fetch failures and control-plane reconnect loops for multiple serving nodes in us-east-1.
- Customer reported degraded tail-latency for streaming sessions and elevated 5xx rates in the Redwood Console during incident windows.
- Affects production traffic for Acadia's private deployment; estimated 12-18% of requests experienced transient auth failures during peak windows.

Environment:
- Redwood Private (VPC peered via TGW) deployed into Acadia's AWS account
- VPCE endpoints for control-plane and S3 presigned artifact fetches
- Egress NAT appliance: on-prem firewall/NAT device performing active reverse-DNS probes and TCP health checks
- TLS: mTLS between agents and control-plane; OCSP stapling enabled on Redwood hosted certs
steps_to_reproduce:
1) From customer VPC serving node, initiate long-running gRPC streams to control-plane while concurrently performing large sharded presigned S3 downloads.
2) Simulate egress appliance blocking PTR lookups (e.g., drop/blackhole TCP/UDP to port 53 for reverse DNS collector) or otherwise rate-limit ICMP/UDP to the collector.
3) Observe: occasional 5xx errors from control-plane, delayed OCSP stapling validation logs, and token refresh attempts in agent logs.
4) Verify by allowing PTR probes: auth failures and OCSP timeouts drop immediately.

comments: 2026-03-10 15:02 - Support (Asha Patel): Acknowledged, opening investigation. Notified SRE team and requested netflow/pcap from customer egress. Assigned to Evelyn.

2026-03-10 17:24 - Customer (J. Morales, Acadia): We see spikes exactly at 14:00-15:30 UTC, correlates with our outbound ACL changes applied by perimeter team. We can temporarily allow additional egress to debug.

2026-03-11 09:40 - SRE (Evelyn Chen): Captured tcpdump on serving node. Observed repeated PTR (reverse) DNS queries to 198.51.100.12 over UDP/53 and TCP/53 followed by SYN to internal collector port; responses inconsistent. Blocking at perimeter results in delayed OCSP fetch retries. Filing as likely middlebox interference.
2026-03-11 12:10 - Customer (J. Morales): Whitelisted the reverse-probe collector and reduced firewall rate-limit. Errors dropped to normal levels. We'll keep monitored for 24h and report back.
2026-03-12 08:03 - Support (Asha Patel): Marking as In Progress while we coordinate permanent mitigation and follow-up runbook updates.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: Egress device performs active reverse-DNS/collector probes and blocks/ratelimits responses leading to OCSP/responder timeouts during cert validation path.
Observed on-packet drops for PTR responses; firewall logs show 'dns_probe_blocked' rules triggered at same timestamps as ocsp timeouts.

RFC behavior: some OCSP responders perform reverse PTR checks or client systems perform reverse lookups for logging/geo->AS inference before contacting upstream and delay validation workflows when PTR hangs; customer appliance was configured to 'inspect' DNS and drop responses when reverse query pattern matched internal heuristics.
We reproduced by simulating blackholed PTR responses: control-plane mTLS fail rate increased by ~15% and OCSP fetch latencies spiked from 40ms to 5s.
No evidence of certificate compromise—failures are timeouts while waiting for revocation info. No model-shard integrity problems detected (only fetch/auth failures).
resolution_notes:
Short-term workaround: Customer perimeter team whitelisted the reverse-DNS collector and relaxed rate-limits on PTR responses; immediate drop in 5xx/mTLS failures observed.

Permanent mitigation plan:
- Update Private deployment runbook to document that egress middleboxes must allow PTR/reverse DNS responses to collectors used by their NAT/appliance for control-plane/OCSP interactions.
- Engineering: Add a fallback to skip reverse PTR-dependent probes in the OCSP fetch path when probes exceed a configurable timeout (tracked in ENG-5872).
- SRE/Support: Provide customer with a recommended egress ACL template and a verification script (dig + tcpdump example) for checking PTR/OCSP reachability.

Follow-up: Create internal knowledge article and notify Solutions Engineers to flag this pattern during onboarding for private deployments.
